title: Visa, Mastercard, Major Banks Facing New Litigation over 'Anticompetitive' Fees
title_zh: Visa、Mastercard 及各大银行因“反竞争”费用面临新诉讼

paragraphs.en: Filed: September 30, 2026 ◆ § 1:26-cv-06087
A class action lawsuit alleges Visa, Mastercard and some of America's largest banks have conspired to artificially inflate merchants' credit card transaction fees.
paragraphs.zh: 一起集体诉讼指控维萨（Visa）、万事达（Mastercard）以及美国一些最大的银行合谋人为抬高商户的信用卡交易手续费。

paragraphs.en: A San Diego pizzeria alleges in a proposed class action lawsuit that Visa, Mastercard and several of the nation’s largest banks have maintained a conspiracy to artificially inflate the fees merchants pay on credit card transactions, despite a more than $5 billion class action settlement in recent years over the same allegedly anticompetitive market restraints.
paragraphs.zh: 一家圣地亚哥披萨店在一项拟议的集体诉讼中指控称，Visa、万事达卡以及美国几家最大的银行一直维持着一阴谋，人为抬高商户在信用卡交易中支付的费用，尽管近年来针对同一所谓反竞争市场限制行为已经达成了一项超过 50 亿美元的集体诉讼和解。

paragraphs.en: The 134-page lawsuit contends that the effectively non-negotiable credit card transaction fees imposed by the defendants amount to “a deadweight toll on virtually every credit card purchase in America,” totaling hundreds of billions in “monopoly rents” at rates that “no competitive market would produce.”
paragraphs.zh: 这份长达134页的诉讼指控称，被告收取的实际上不可协商的信用卡交易手续费相当于“对美国几乎所有信用卡消费征收的一种无谓过路费”，总额高达数千亿美元的“垄断租金”，且其费率“在任何竞争性市场中都不会产生”。

paragraphs.en: According to the complaint, Visa and Mastercard have worked with the bank defendants— Bank of America , Capital One , Chase Bank , Citibank and Wells Fargo —for decades to set uniform schedules of interchange fees, i.e., the effectively non-negotiable charges merchants must pay to credit card-issuing banks on each transaction. The case charges that the defendants, to maintain the high interchange fees and “ensure merchants cannot escape them,” have implemented a “web of anticompetitive rules,” or restraints, that on the whole have disabled any market forces that could rein in or otherwise discipline the credit card transaction costs imposed on merchants.
paragraphs.zh: 根据诉状，Visa 和 Mastercard 数十年来一直与被告银行——美国银行、Capital One、大通银行、花旗银行和富国银行——合作设定统一的交换费标准，即商户在每笔交易中必须向信用卡发卡银行支付的实际上不可议价的费用。 该案指控被告为维持高额交换费并“确保商户无法逃避这些费用”，实施了一套“反竞争规则网络”（即各种限制措施），总体上使任何能够遏制或约束强加给商户的信用卡交易成本的市场力量失去了作用。

sents.en: According to the complaint, Visa and Mastercard have worked with the bank defendants— Bank of America , Capital One , Chase Bank , Citibank and Wells Fargo —for decades to set uniform schedules of interchange fees, i.e., the effectively non-negotiable charges merchants must pay to credit card-issuing banks on each transaction.
sents.zh: 根据诉状，Visa 和 Mastercard 数十年来一直与被告银行——美国银行、Capital One、大通银行、花旗银行和富国银行——合作设定统一的交换费标准，即商户在每笔交易中必须向信用卡发卡银行支付的实际上不可议价的费用。

sents.en: The case charges that the defendants, to maintain the high interchange fees and “ensure merchants cannot escape them,” have implemented a “web of anticompetitive rules,” or restraints, that on the whole have disabled any market forces that could rein in or otherwise discipline the credit card transaction costs imposed on merchants.
sents.zh: 该案指控被告为维持高额交换费并“确保商户无法逃避这些费用”，实施了一套“反竞争规则网络”（即各种限制措施），总体上使任何能够遏制或约束强加给商户的信用卡交易成本的市场力量失去了作用。

paragraphs.en: Broadly, the interlocking restraints set and maintained by the defendants have forced merchants that accept any Visa and Mastercard credit card to accept all such cards, regardless of cost, thereby eliminating any incentive for issuing banks to compete by lowering their fees, the suit says. The lawsuit claims the challenged restraints have also prevented merchants from being able to steer customers to lower-cost payment options —for instance, by surcharging based on a customer’s use of a particular card. These and other restraints have prevented competition among issuing banks and other credit card networks, allowing the financial giants to raise their fees every year “without consequence,” the case alleges.
paragraphs.zh: 诉讼称，总的来说，被告设置并维持的相互交织的限制措施，迫使接受任何 Visa 和 Mastercard 信用卡的商户接受所有此类信用卡，而不论成本高低，从而消除了发卡银行通过降低费用展开竞争的任何动力。 诉讼称，受到质疑的限制措施还使商户无法引导顾客使用成本更低的支付方式，例如，根据顾客使用的特定卡种收取附加费。 案件指控称，这些及其他限制措施阻碍了发卡银行与其他信用卡网络之间的竞争，使这些金融巨头得以每年提高费用而“不承担任何后果”。

sents.en: Broadly, the interlocking restraints set and maintained by the defendants have forced merchants that accept any Visa and Mastercard credit card to accept all such cards, regardless of cost, thereby eliminating any incentive for issuing banks to compete by lowering their fees, the suit says.
sents.zh: 诉讼称，总的来说，被告设置并维持的相互交织的限制措施，迫使接受任何 Visa 和 Mastercard 信用卡的商户接受所有此类信用卡，而不论成本高低，从而消除了发卡银行通过降低费用展开竞争的任何动力。

sents.en: The lawsuit claims the challenged restraints have also prevented merchants from being able to steer customers to lower-cost payment options —for instance, by surcharging based on a customer’s use of a particular card.
sents.zh: 诉讼称，受到质疑的限制措施还使商户无法引导顾客使用成本更低的支付方式，例如，根据顾客使用的特定卡种收取附加费。

sents.en: These and other restraints have prevented competition among issuing banks and other credit card networks, allowing the financial giants to raise their fees every year “without consequence,” the case alleges.
sents.zh: 案件指控称，这些及其他限制措施阻碍了发卡银行与其他信用卡网络之间的竞争，使这些金融巨头得以每年提高费用而“不承担任何后果”。

paragraphs.en: “The scale of this ongoing scheme is staggering: merchants now pay over $100 billion annually in fees to accept Visa and Mastercard credit cards, enriching Defendants at merchants’ expense,” the class action lawsuit states.
paragraphs.zh: “这场持续进行的阴谋规模惊人：商家目前每年需支付超过1000亿美元的费用才能受理Visa和Mastercard信用卡，令被告以牺牲商家利益为代价中饱私囊，”该集体诉讼称。

paragraphs.en: The filing claims Visa and Mastercard have also exploited the allegedly anticompetitive market handcuffs to artificially inflate their own network fees—comprised of per-transaction fees and fixed fees—charged to merchants as a cost of accepting the companies’ credit cards, adding “an additional supracompetitive tax on each credit card transaction.”
paragraphs.zh: 起诉书声称，Visa 和 Mastercard 还利用了这种据称具有反竞争性质的市场束缚，人为抬升向商户收取的网络费用（包括每笔交易费用和固定费用）——这是商户接受这两家公司信用卡所需承担的成本——从而“在每笔信用卡交易上额外征收了一种超出竞争水平的税”。

paragraphs.en: The suit states that in December 2019, the court approved a class action settlement in years-old multidistrict litigation that provided upward of $5 billion in monetary relief to merchants, but only for a “class period” ending on January 24, 2019. Although a separate “equitable relief” class action settlement seeking injunctive relief has been preliminarily approved, the benefits will apply only prospectively and merchants will not receive “a single dollar in compensation ... for the fees they have paid since January 25, 2019.”
paragraphs.zh: 该诉讼称，2019年12月，法院批准了一项多年前的多区合并诉讼（multidistrict litigation）的集体诉讼和解方案，该方案为商户提供了超过50亿美元的货币救济，但仅适用于截止日期为2019年1月24日的“集体期间”。 尽管寻求禁令救济的另一项“衡平救济”集体诉讼和解已获初步批准，但其益处仅面向未来适用，商户将不会“就其自2019年1月25日以来所支付的费用获得哪怕一美元的补偿”。

sents.en: The suit states that in December 2019, the court approved a class action settlement in years-old multidistrict litigation that provided upward of $5 billion in monetary relief to merchants, but only for a “class period” ending on January 24, 2019.
sents.zh: 该诉讼称，2019年12月，法院批准了一项多年前的多区合并诉讼（multidistrict litigation）的集体诉讼和解方案，该方案为商户提供了超过50亿美元的货币救济，但仅适用于截止日期为2019年1月24日的“集体期间”。

sents.en: Although a separate “equitable relief” class action settlement seeking injunctive relief has been preliminarily approved, the benefits will apply only prospectively and merchants will not receive “a single dollar in compensation ... for the fees they have paid since January 25, 2019.”
sents.zh: 尽管寻求禁令救济的另一项“衡平救济”集体诉讼和解已获初步批准，但其益处仅面向未来适用，商户将不会“就其自2019年1月25日以来所支付的费用获得哪怕一美元的补偿”。

paragraphs.en: According to the complaint, while some merchants obtained relief for pre-2019 transactions and some may benefit from rule changes in the future, merchants that accepted Visa and Mastercard credit cards after January 2019 have “borne the full brunt of Defendants’ continuing anticompetitive conduct.”
paragraphs.zh: 根据起诉书，虽然部分商户就2019年之前的交易获得了救济，部分商户未来可能从规则变更中受益，但在2019年1月之后受理Visa和Mastercard信用卡的商户却“承受了被告持续反竞争行为带来的全部冲击”。

paragraphs.en: “This settlement structure leaves millions of American merchants without any remedy for their ongoing injuries,” the lawsuit attests.
paragraphs.zh: “这种和解结构使数百万美国商户对其持续受到的损害得不到任何救济，”诉状中陈述道。

paragraphs.en: The interchange fees class action lawsuit looks to represent all individuals, businesses and other entities that have accepted Visa-branded and/or Mastercard-branded credit cards in the United States from January 25, 2019 until the alleged “anticompetitive effects” of the defendants’ conduct cease.
paragraphs.zh: 交换费集体诉讼旨在代表自2019年1月25日起至被告行为的所谓「反竞争影响」停止期间，在美国受理过Visa品牌和/或Mastercard品牌信用卡的所有个人、企业及其他实体。

paragraphs.en: If your child suffers from video game addiction — including Fortnite addiction or Roblox addiction — you may be able to take legal action. Gamers 18 to 22 may also qualify.
paragraphs.zh: 如果您的孩子沉迷于电子游戏——包括沉迷《堡垒之夜》或《Roblox》——您或许可以采取法律行动。 18 至 22 岁的游戏玩家也可能符合条件。

paragraphs.en: Anyone who has used 7-OH kratom products and suffered a serious injury, such as overdose, heart attack or addiction, may be able to take legal action.
paragraphs.zh: 任何曾使用过 7-OH 卡痛（kratom）产品并遭受严重伤害（如过量、心脏病发作或成瘾）的人，都可能可以采取法律行动。

paragraphs.en: Did you know there's usually nothing you need to do to join, sign up for, or add your name to new class action lawsuits when they're initially filed?
paragraphs.zh: 你知道吗？新的集体诉讼最初提起时，通常你无需做任何事情即可加入、注册或将其名字列入其中。
